_comment: Curated note -> axis mapping, authored judgment committed for review
(same precedent as data/blocklist.txt: open it and argue with it).
Loaded by fragrance_graph.notes.load_note_axes, which re-checks every
entry against 'SELECT DISTINCT canonical_note FROM fragrance_note_claim'
at load time and drops anything the corpus no longer carries.
Every entry below was checked exact-case-insensitive against that
query before this file was written; nothing here is a substring or
family guess ('amber' does NOT pull in 'ambergris' -- they are
different rows and stay different notes). Six candidates from the
original brief did not survive that check and are deliberately
absent: clove, sugar, chocolate, cucumber, sea salt, aquatic notes --
the corpus's fragrance_note_claim table has no canonical_note equal
to any of those strings (it has 'cloves', 'brown sugar', 'cocoa',
'aquatic accord' etc., which are different rows, not variants of
these words, so they are not silently substituted in here).
A note may belong to more than one axis (vanilla is warm AND sweet
AND gourmand). An axis absent from a request (or a request naming an
axis not below) subtracts nothing beyond the literal word typed --
see load_note_axes.

2026-08-17: boozy notes (rum, cognac, whiskey/whisky, bourbon) added to warm after 'side effect but too warm' kept rum in the profile; axis entries match by token containment, so an entry may claim corpus variants beyond its exact string.
2026-08-18 (catalog-first spec): five families added --
gourmand/citrus/woody/floral/aquatic -- for
fragrance_graph.catalog_profile, which derives a per-bottle
CATALOG-DERIVED family tendency (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, from declared-note
counts only, never a comment) and an occasion prior from it. These
are curated the identical way warm/sweet/fresh were: a short,
checked word list, not a family-guess substring rule, re-verified
against the corpus below (survivor counts as of 2026-08-18, 548
fragrances / 411 with any declared note):
citrus    11 entries -> 95 corpus notes matched, 0 dropped
woody     11 entries -> 91 corpus notes matched, 0 dropped
floral    16 entries -> 165 corpus notes matched, 0 dropped
gourmand  11 entries -> 94 corpus notes matched, 0 dropped
aquatic    3 entries -> 6 corpus notes matched, 0 dropped
Deliberate overlaps with the original three, documented rather than
silently duplicated: 'gourmand' extends 'sweet' with more
dessert/food notes (vanilla, caramel, praline, honey, tonka bean are
in both -- 'sweet' is the narrower dessert-adjacent-smell axis,
'gourmand' is the broader edible-catalog-tendency one the spec asks
for). 'citrus' and 'aquatic' are new, narrower complements to the
existing 'fresh' axis (which already carries bergamot/lemon/lime/
grapefruit/mandarin/neroli/mint/apple/green notes) rather than
replacements for it -- 'fresh' is kept exactly as it was so nothing
already depending on it (recommend._anchor_profile_fallback's 'too
warm'/'too fresh' subtraction) changes meaning; the occasion-prior
rule below reads citrus, aquatic AND fresh together for exactly this
reason. 'woody' and 'floral' are wholly new families with no prior
axis to overlap. 'chocolate' and 'kumquat' were tried and dropped by
the same corpus check as the original six (the corpus has 'cocoa'
and 'chinese kumquats', not those exact strings) -- 'cocoa' and
'kumquats' are what is actually below.
'occasion_priors' (below the axes) is metadata, not an axis -- see
its own inline note and load_note_axes'/load_occasion_priors'
docstrings for why it is skipped by the axis loader.
ONE documented, conservative rule table -- not one rule invented
per occasion in code. Read by
fragrance_graph.catalog_profile.load_occasion_priors, which pulls
this key out whole (no per-note corpus revalidation: this table
names AXES, already checked above, not literal notes) and is
deliberately skipped by notes.load_note_axes (it is not itself a
note -> axis mapping and must never be treated as one).
Each occasion names 'high_if_any_high' (the bottle's declared
profile is a plausible catalog fit for this occasion when AT LEAST
ONE of these family tendencies is HIGH) and 'low_required' (AND
none of these are HIGH -- a citrus-forward bottle that is ALSO
gourmand-forward is not a clean summer prior, it is two things at
once, and the honest answer is silence, not a claim either way).
MEDIUM never counts as HIGH on either side -- deliberately
conservative, per the spec: a maybe-fresh, maybe-not bottle earns
no occasion prior rather than a stretched one.
Only 'summer' is curated today. An occasion with no entry here
gets no catalog-derived prior at all (catalog_profile.
occasion_prior returns None) -- silence, the same MISSING DATA
answer this codebase gives everywhere else, never a guessed rule.
